newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols ascend with spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols ascend with spot.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options were strongly higher in U.S. trading after the spot mounted an assault on 1.82 marks in Europe.
"It seems like a knee-jerk reaction to the spot move," said one U.S. options trader.

After opening firm in the U.S. at 10.65/10.75 percent, one-month dollar/mark volatility continued well bid, gaining an additional 0.1 percentage point by midday, said a New York-based broker. From late Monday, the one-month bid is up 0.75 percentage point.
The one-month 25-delta risk reversal widened to 0.7/1.0 favoring mark puts from 0.3/0.6.
Persistent sentiment the euro will be a soft currency propelled the dollar to a fresh 71-month peak at 1.8197 marks.
Options traders called the rise in volatility relatively restrained given that spot dollar/mark broke above its range.
"There doesn't seem to be an overreaction," said the New York broker. "We're waiting to see if we can sustain the dollar above 1.82 against the mark."
Such a move could ignite volatility in the pair, driving away potential sellers, traders said. But for now, they noted, activity in the spot was overshadowing everything else.
"There has been no leap into buying options," said the New York broker.

In addition to worrying about whether dollar strength is sustainable, market participants are reluctant to establish positions before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony is heard, traders said. Greenspan will present his views on monetary policy and the U.S. economy before a House subcommittee starting at 1400 EDT.
The volatile U.S. stock market is another wildcard.
Traders said interest was concentrated in the very short dates and in the longer dates.
One-year dollar/mark volatility climbed to 10.5/10.6 percent from 10.0/10.3 quoted late Monday.
In dollar/yen, market talk attributed pressure on the spot dollar to a large foreign bank's defense of a knockout option with an upside trigger at 116.50 yen.

One-month dollar/yen volatility rose 0.3 percentage point to 10.0/10.3 percent and one-year gained 0.1 point to 10.7/10.9 percent. One-month risk reversals retained a slight skew for yen calls at 0.4/0.6, unchanged from the previous day.
